AtlaSlope

Map tour round 1

Four directions for the Rioja tour. Same four stops in each, real satellite and real photos, desktop and phone. Map and photo frames are captured from the app; the screens around them are design drawn for this round.

What we are after

  • The reader sets the pace. One beat per screen, nothing moves while they read.
  • Wide first, then tight and tilted. Every stop is composed, not "the pin somewhere in the middle".
  • One slow move per beat, about 3 s. Arriving matters more than flying.
  • The photo is the close-up. The satellite shows where, the photo shows the ground.
  • The text is a caption. One short sentence on screen, the rest in the guide.
  • What broke in 61-62: the map shrank to a side panel, the stop cards and photos went, and the map flew mid-paragraph.

1Still guide

No tour. The guide is the product: each place gets a photo and a small map picture beside the text. Nothing flies, nothing jumps.

Camera. There is no camera move. Each picture is fixed; "Open the map" leaves the guide for the atlas.

Desktop

Phone

2Guide plus "Fly the tour"

Close to release 59. The guide opens with a large entry and a photo. One press starts a full-screen tour, one card per stop.

Camera. Eases to each stop with one 3 s glide when you press Next; holds still while you read the card. You press, so it never moves on its own.

Desktop

Phone

3ScenesRecommended

The guide reads as four scenes, one per screen. The photo leads, the sentence sits under it, the map is the stage beside it. The map follows the scene you scroll to.

Camera. Holds while you read; one 3 s glide at the scene turn, only when a scene snaps into place, never mid-paragraph. Wide first, then tight and tilted.

Desktop

Phone

4Film

A play button and then the map takes over. It flies, the photo fades in, a subtitle says one line. Close it to return to the guide.

Camera. Continuous: glide 3 s, hold 6 s, glide on. Photo fades in 1 s after arrival and out before the next glide. Pause stops everything.

Desktop

Phone

Pick one

  • 1 Still guide. Cheapest and calmest. No cinema.
  • 2 Fly the tour. Safest step from release 59. Cinematic only when pressed.
  • 3 Scenes (recommended). The map stays in step with the text and never jumps. Photo leads on every stop.
  • 4 Film. Most cinematic. Most to build, and the reader gives up the pace.
